title: Efficient Modeling of Multi-Agent Systems via Structure-Aware Physics-Informed Learning
abstract: arXiv:2611.21404v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Modeling large multi-agent systems poses challenges for trajectory inference and parameter identification, as network size and coupling increase computational demands and partial observations require reconstructing unobserved states. We propose MAS-PINN, a neural-network architecture with a tailored training algorithm for a physics-informed learning framework that leverages the network topology and the agents' similarity to reduce computational and memory costs of simulating and identifying multi-agent systems. Its architecture represents agent trajectories through shared temporal features and agent-specific coefficients. Training alternates between learning features, fitting coupled trajectories, and estimating physical parameters. A matrix-free update exploits local interactions to fit trajectories without forming large global matrices. translated_title: 基于结构感知的物理信息学习实现多智能体系统的高效建模
translated_abstract: 对大规模多智能体系统进行建模，在轨迹推断与参数辨识方面面临挑战，因为网络规模与耦合程度的增加会带来更高的计算需求，而部分观测则要求重构未被观测到的状态。我们提出MAS-PINN，这是一种面向物理信息学习框架的神经网络架构及配套训练算法，利用网络拓扑结构和智能体之间的相似性来降低多智能体系统仿真与辨识的计算和内存成本。该架构通过共享的时间特征与各智能体专属的系数来表示智能体轨迹。训练过程在学习特征、拟合耦合轨迹和估计物理参数之间交替进行。一种无矩阵更新方法利用局部交互来拟合轨迹，无需构建大型全局矩阵。在洛伦兹环、洛特卡-沃尔泰拉网络和若斯勒振荡器上的实验表明，轨迹估计与参数辨识性能得到提升。
tldr: 该论文提出MAS-PINN，一种利用网络拓扑与智能体相似性、结合共享时间特征表示和无矩阵更新策略的物理信息神经网络架构，显著降低了大规模多智能体系统轨迹推断与参数辨识的计算和内存成本。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes MAS-PINN, a physics-informed neural network architecture that leverages network topology and agent similarity through shared temporal features and a matrix-free update strategy to significantly reduce the computational and memory costs of trajectory inference and parameter identification in large multi-agent systems.
